9.?

Find where the normal line to the curve f(x)=3x2−4x+1 at the point (2,5) intersects the y-axis.

E
Fri, Jul 24th @ 11:43 PM|Elapsed: 7:53Correct

Taking the derivative, we have

f′(x)=ddx(3x2−4x+1)=6x−4.

So the slope of the tangent line is m=f′(2)=6(2)−4=8, and therefore the slope of the normal line is m′=−1m=−18.

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

y−5=−18(x−2)y=−18x+14+5y=−18x+214.

Lastly, we find the point of intersection with the y-axis by setting x=0 and solving the resulting equation. We get y=−18⋅0+214y=214.

Therefore, the normal line intersects the y-axis at (0,214).

10.?

Fri, Jul 24th @ 11:46 PM|Elapsed: 2:27Correct

Taking the derivative, we have

f′(x)=ddx(x2)=2x. So the slope of the tangent line is m=f′(3)=2(3)=6, and therefore the slope of the normal line is m′=−1m=−16. Finally, the equation of the normal line is

y−9=−16(x−3)y=−16x+12+9y=−16x+192.

Lastly, we find the point of intersection with the x-axis by setting y=0 and solving the resulting equation. We get −16x+192=0192=16xx=57. Therefore, the normal line intersects the x-axis at (57,0).
